# Swiss Data Events: all upcoming events

> Swiss Data Events (swissdataevents.ch) is a curated list of upcoming AI and data events in Switzerland: meetups, conferences, workshops, networking evenings and webinars about Databricks, Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, the Azure data platform, AI strategy and governance, data governance, data leadership and applied AI. Every listing is checked against the organiser's own page before it is published, and the list is refreshed every day. Registration always happens on the organiser's site.

Last checked against sources: 2026-11-28T14:04:08Z. 163 upcoming events. All times are Europe/Zurich. These lists are rebuilt every day with only the events that had not ended on that date: if the date is more than two days old, you are reading a cached copy, so fetch it again.

Shorter lists per city and event type are linked from [llms.txt](https://swissdataevents.ch/llms.txt). The same events as structured data: [events.json](https://swissdataevents.ch/events.json).

## Upcoming events

### Already running

- [Hack Apertus — Onsite Hackathon Zurich](https://swissdataevents.ch/events/hack-apertus-onsite-zurich-2026/): 27 Nov 2026 – 28 Nov 2026 · AI Startup Center, Technopark Zürich, Zurich · Workshop · Not listed · by AI Startup Center. The on-site leg of the national Apertus hackathon: build on the open Apertus 8B model, strengthen its multilingual abilities and ship applications for private- and public-sector problems, with everything released as Open Commons.

### December 2026

Fourth edition of HSLU’s AIristoteles series: an EPFL evolutionary psychologist and a psychotherapist discuss what it means when people enter long-term relationships with AI bots, moderated by Stephan Klapproth and followed by an apéro.

Final Bern meetup of the year for the Swiss AWS community: a mix of community talks plus discussion and networking, with the agenda announced closer to the date.

IBM’s Ethan Mendel explains why general-purpose AI models become unreliable on mainframe-scale codebases, and how static code analysis combined with metadata-enriched models makes AI dependable for modernisation work.

A German-language breakfast session with Quatico CEO Jan Wloka on why adding more AI agents tends to produce more review work than finished work, and the three changes that fixed it for his team: a written decision before any agent starts coding, work split into packages that run in parallel, and one daily overview of what needs a human. Aimed at product owners and delivery leads, with a real work package run live.
